'''Vladimir (Vlad) M. Shalaev''' is a Distinguished Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering<ref name="Disting. Prof.">[https://engineering.purdue.edu/ECE/People/ptProfile?resource_id=3322 People, School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Purdue University]</ref> and Scientific Director for Nanophotonics at Birck Nanotechnology Center,<ref>[http://www.purdue.edu/discoverypark/birck/directory/directory.php?group_id=147364 Birck Nanotechnology Center Faculty]</ref> [[Purdue University]].

==Education and career==
V. Shalaev earned a [[Master of Science]] Degree in physics (summa cum laude) in 1979 from [[Krasnoyarsk State University]] ([[Russia]]) and a PhD Degree in physics and mathematics in 1983 from the same university. Over the course of his career, Shalaev received a number of awards for his research in the fields of [[nanophotonics]] and [[metamaterial]]s, and he is a Fellow of  several of Professional Societies (see the Awards, honors, memberships section below). Prof. Shalaev (with his [[h-index]] of 132, as of January 2026, and 77,000 citations, in total,
according to Google Scholar<ref name="Google Scolar">[https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=uKn4q1sAAAAJ Shalaev h-index and citations, Google Scholar]</ref>) has nearly 1,000 publications in the field of science and technology, including
1 monograph and 2 co-authored books, 4 edited/co-edited books, 30 invited book chapters, and 50 USA patents.<ref name="Pubs list">[https://engineering.purdue.edu/~shalaev/Publication_list.php V. Shalaev's publication list]</ref> He is ranked #29 in electronics and electrical engineering among the USA researchers and #50 worldwide, according to Research.com website.<ref name="Research.com-rankings">[https://research.com/scientists-rankings/electronics-and-electrical-engineering Research.com Scientists Rankings - Electronics and Eelectrical Engineering]</ref> Prof. Shalaev is ranked #22 in the  “optics” category out of ~ 80,000 entries in the Stanford list of top 2% world’s highest-cited scientists (career-long).<ref name="topresearcherslist">[https://topresearcherslist.com/Home/Profile/765306 Shalaev, Vladimir M. - TopResearchersList.com]</ref> He is also recognized as Highly Cited Researcher (in physics) by the [[Web of Science]] Group for eight consecutive years, in 2017-2024.<ref name="WebOfScience">[https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/1282341 Vladimir M. Shalaev on WebOfScience.com]</ref>

==Research==

Vladimir M. Shalaev is recognized for his pioneering studies on linear and [[nonlinear optics]] of random [[Nanophotonics|nanophotonic]] composites that had helped to mold the research area of composite optical media.<ref name="Lamb award">[http://www.lambaward.org/2010/2010-shalaev.html 2010 Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics]</ref> He also contributed to the emergence of a new field of engineered, artificial materials - optical metamaterials.<ref name="Max Born Award">[https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/maxborn/ 2010 Optical Society of America Max Born Award]</ref><ref name="Lamb award" /> Currently, he studies new phenomena resulting from merging metamaterials and plasmonics with quantum nanophotonics.<ref name="quantum decoherence">S. I. Bogdanov, A. Boltasseva, V. M. Shalaev, [https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aax3766 Overcoming quantum decoherence with plasmonics], Science, v. 364, no. 6440, pp. 532-533 (2019)</ref>

===Optical metamaterials===
[[Photonic metamaterial|Optical metamaterials]] (MMs) are rationally designed composite nanostructured materials that exhibit unique electromagnetic properties drastically different from the properties of their constituent material components. Metamaterials offer remarkable tailorability of their electromagnetic response via shape, size, composition and morphology of their nanoscale building blocks sometimes called 'meta-atoms'.<ref>N. Meinzer, W.L. Barnes & I.R. Hooper, [https://www.nature.com/articles/nphoton.2014.247 Plasmonic meta-atoms and metasurfaces], N. Meinzer, William L. Barnes & I.R. Hooper, Nature Photonics, v. 8, pp. 889–898 (2014)</ref> Shalaev proposed and demonstrated the first optical MM that exhibits negative index of refraction and the nanostructures that show artificial magnetism across the entire visible spectrum.<ref name="Optical Negative-Index Metamaterials">V.M. Shalaev,  [https://engineering.purdue.edu/~shalaev/Publication_list_files/Optical%20negative-index%20metamaterials.pdf Optical Negative-Index Metamaterials], Nature photonics, v. 1, pp. 41–48 (2007)</ref><ref name="Negative Index of Refraction in Optical Metamaterials">V.M. Shalaev, W. Cai, U.K. Chettiar, H.-K. Yuan, A.K. Sarychev, V.P. Drachev, and A.V. Kildishev, [https://engineering.purdue.edu/~shalaev/Publication_list_files/OLpaper.pdf Negative Index of Refraction in Optical Metamaterials], Optics Letters, v. 30, pp. 3356–3358 (2005); [https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0504091 arxiv.org/abs/physics/0504091] (April 13, 2005)</ref><ref name="Optical Metamaterials: Fundamentals and Applications">W. Cai, V.M. Shalaev, [https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9781441911506 Optical Metamaterials: Fundamentals and Applications], Springer-Verlag, New York (2010)</ref><ref name="Metamagnetics with rainbow colors">W. Sarychev.<ref name="name_19" /><ref name="name_21" /><ref name="name_22" /><ref name="name_26" /> Shalaev also developed fundamental theories of surface-enhanced [[Raman scattering]] (SERS) and strongly-enhanced optical nonlinearities in fractals and percolation systems and led experimental studies aimed to verify the developed theories.<ref name="name_18" /><sup>−</sup><ref name="name_28" /><ref name="name_31" /><ref>M. Shalaev’s contributions to the optics and plasmonics of random media<ref name="name_18" /><sup>−</sup><ref name="name_28" /> helped transform those concepts into the area of optical metamaterials.<ref name="Optical Negative-Index Metamaterials" /><sup>−</sup><ref name="Metamagnetics with rainbow colors" /><ref name=":0" /><sup>−</sup><ref name=":1" /> Owing to the theory and experimental approaches developed in the area of random composites, optical metamaterials have become a mature research field rich in new physics.<ref name="Optical Metamaterials: Fundamentals and Applications" /><ref name="Landauer Award">[https://engineering.purdue.edu/~shalaev/ETOPIM%20Landauer%20Medal.pdf 2015 Rolf Landauer International ETOPIM Association Medal]</ref> Shalaev’s impact on the development of both fields is in identifying the strong synergy and close connection between these two frontier fields of optics that unlock an entirely new set of physical properties.<ref name="Landauer Award" />

===New Materials for Nanophotonics and Plasmonics===

Random composites and metamaterials provide a unique opportunity to tailor their optical properties via shape, size and composition of their nanoscale building blocks, which often require metals to confine light down to the nanometer scale via the excitation of surface plasmons.<ref name="name_18" /><ref name="Active nanoplasmonic metamaterials"/> To enable practical applications of plasmonics, Shalaev in collaboration with [[Alexandra Boltasseva|A. Boltasseva]]<ref>[https://engineering.purdue.edu/~aeb/index.shtml Prof. A. Boltasseva's research group site]</ref> developed novel plasmonic materials, namely [[transition metal]] nitrides and transparent conducting oxides (TCOs), paving the way to durable, low-loss, and CMOS-compatible plasmonic and nanophotonic devices.<ref name="name_35">P.R. West, S. Ishii, G.V. Naik, N.K. Emani, V.M. Shalaev, and A. Boltasseva, [https://engineering.purdue.edu/~shalaev/Publication_list_files/lpor_200900055_a.pdf Searching for better plasmonic materials], Laser & Photonics Reviews, v. 4, pp. 795–808 (2010)</ref><ref name="name_36">G.V. Naik, V.M. Shalaev, and A. Boltasseva, [https://engineering.purdue.edu/~shalaev/Publication_list_files/Naik_AdvMater2013-2.pdf Alternative Plasmonic Materials: Beyond Gold and Silver], Advanced Materials, v. 25, pp. 3264–3294 (2013)</ref><ref name="name_37">U. Guler, A. Boltasseva, and V. M. Shalaev, [https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1252722 Refractory plasmonics], Science, v. 344, pp. 263–264 (2014)</ref><ref name="name_38">U. Guler, V.M. Shalaev, A. Boltasseva, [https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1369702114004106 Nanoparticle Plasmonics: Going Practical with Transition Metal Nitrides], Materials Today, v. 18, pp. 227–237 (2014)</ref><ref name="name_39">U. Guler, A. Kildishev, A. Boltasseva, and V.M. Shalaev, [http://pubs.rsc.org/en/Content/ArticleLanding/2015/FD/C4FD00208C#!divAbstract Plasmonics on the slope of enlightenment: the role of transition metal nitrides], Faraday Discussions, v. 178, pp. 71–86 (2015)</ref><ref name="name_40">A. Boltasseva and V.M. Shalaev, [https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aaa8282 All that glitters need not be gold], Science, v. 347, pp. 1308-1310 (2015)</ref><ref name="name_41">A. Naldoni, U. Guler, Zh. Wang, M. Marelli, F. Malara, X. Meng, A.V. Kildishev, A. Boltasseva, V.M. Shalaev, [http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/adom.201601031/full Broadband Hot Electron Collection for Solar Water Splitting with Plasmonic Titanium Nitride], Advanced Optical Materials,  v. 5, p. 1601031 (2017)</ref> The proposed plasmonic ceramics operating at high temperatures, can offer solutions to highly efficient energy conversion, photocatalysis and data storage technologies<ref name="name_37" /><sup>−</sup>.<ref name="name_41" /> In collaboration with the Faccio group,<ref>[http://extremelight.eps.hw.ac.uk/ Prof. D. Faccio group, Heriot-Watt University, UK]</ref> Shalaev demonstrated ultrafast, strongly-enhanced nonlinear responses in TCOs that possess an extremely low (close to zero) linear [[refractive index]] – the so-called epsilon-near-zero regime.<ref name="name_42">L. Caspani, R.P.M. Kaipurath, M. Clerici, M. Ferrera, T. Roger, A. Di Falco, J. Kim, N. Kinsey, V. M. Shalaev, A. Boltasseva, D. Faccio, [https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.233901 Enhanced Nonlinear Refractive Index in ε-Near-Zero Materials], Physical Review Letters, v. 116, p. 233901 (2016)</ref><ref name="name_43">M. ===Early research===

Shalaev’s PhD work (supervised by Prof. A.K. Popov) and early research involved theoretical analysis of resonant interaction of laser radiation with gaseous media, in particular i) Doppler-free multi-photon processes in strong optical fields and their applications in nonlinear optics<ref name="name_46">A.K. Popov, V.M. Shalaev, [http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0030401880902072 Doppler-free transitions induced by strong double-frequency optical excitations], Optics Communications, v. 35, pp. 189–193 (1980)</ref> spectroscopy<ref name="name_47">A.K. Popov, V.M. Shalaev, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF00886488 Doppler-free spectroscopy and wave-front conjugation by four-wave mixing of nonmonochromatic waves], Applied Physics, v.21, pp. 93–94 (1980)</ref> and laser physics<ref name="name_48">A.K. Popov, V.M. Shalaev, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF00697298 Unidirectional Doppler-Free Gain And Generation In Optically Pumped Lasers], Applied Physics B, v. 27, pp. 63–67 (1982)</ref> as well as ii) the (newly-discovered then) phenomenon of light-induced drift of gases.<ref name="name_49">A.K. Popov, A.M. Shalagin, V.M. Shalaev, V.Z. Yakhnin, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007%2FBF00902993 Drift of gases induced by nonmonochromatic light], Applied physics, v.25, pp. 347–350 (1981)</ref><ref name="name_50">V.M. Shalaev and V.Z. Yakhnin, [http://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0022-3700/20/12/019 LID sound generated by pulsed excitation in gases], Journal of Physics B: Atomic and Molecular Physics, v.20, pp. 2733–2743 (1987)</ref>

Prof. Shalaev co-/authored three-<ref name="Optical Metamaterials: Fundamentals and Applications" /><ref name="name_20" /><ref name="name_22" /> and co-/edited four<ref>S. Kawata, V.M. Shalaev (editors), [http://store.elsevier.com/product.jsp?isbn=9780444520586&pagename=search Tip Enhancement], Elsevier (2007)</ref><ref>S. Kawata, V.M. He made over 500 invited presentations at International Conferences and leading research centers, including a number of plenary and keynote talks.<ref>[https://engineering.purdue.edu/~shalaev/Conference_presentations.php Prof. V.
